description: Pi-hole-style view of Blocky's query log out of Loki: who is asking, what is blocked, and what is served from cache rather than resolved.

panels.title: Queries
panels.description: Every query the selected resolver(s) answered in the dashboard time range, after the client filter.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({job="blocky", host=~"$host"} | pattern "<_>	<client_ip>	<client_name>	<duration_ms>	<reason>	<question>	<_>" | client_name =~ `(?i).*$client.*` [$__range]))

panels.title: Blocked
panels.description: Queries answered from a blocklist rather than resolved.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({job="blocky", host=~"$host"} |= "BLOCKED" | pattern "<_>	<client_ip>	<client_name>	<duration_ms>	<reason>	<question>	<_>" | client_name =~ `(?i).*$client.*` | reason =~ `BLOCKED.*` [$__range]))

panels.title: Block rate
panels.description: Blocked as a share of all queries.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({job="blocky", host=~"$host"} |= "BLOCKED" | pattern "<_>	<client_ip>	<client_name>	<duration_ms>	<reason>	<question>	<_>" | client_name =~ `(?i).*$client.*` | reason =~ `BLOCKED.*` [$__range])) / sum(count_over_time({job="blocky", host=~"$host"} | pattern "<_>	<client_ip>	<client_name>	<duration_ms>	<reason>	<question>	<_>" | client_name =~ `(?i).*$client.*` [$__range])) * 100

panels.title: Served from cache
panels.description: Share of the queries that actually needed an answer (i.e. excluding blocked ones) that Blocky served from its own cache instead of asking anything upstream. CACHED NEGATIVE counts as a hit.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({job="blocky", host=~"$host"} |= "CACHED" | pattern "<_>	<client_ip>	<client_name>	<duration_ms>	<reason>	<question>	<_>" | client_name =~ `(?i).*$client.*` | reason =~ `CACHED.*` [$__range])) / sum(count_over_time({job="blocky", host=~"$host"} | pattern "<_>	<client_ip>	<client_name>	<duration_ms>	<reason>	<question>	<_>" | client_name =~ `(?i).*$client.*` | reason !~ `BLOCKED.*` [$__range])) * 100

panels.title: Clients
panels.description: Distinct client names seen in the range.

targets.expr: count(sum by (client_name) (count_over_time({job="blocky", host=~"$host"} | pattern "<_>	<client_ip>	<client_name>	<duration_ms>	<reason>	<question>	<_>" | client_name =~ `(?i).*$client.*` [$__range])))

panels.title: p95 lookup
panels.description: 95th percentile of Blocky's own duration column, over real lookups only — blocked and cached answers are 0 ms and would flatter it.

targets.expr: quantile_over_time(0.95, {job="blocky", host=~"$host"} | pattern "<_>	<client_ip>	<client_name>	<duration_ms>	<reason>	<question>	<_>" | client_name =~ `(?i).*$client.*` | reason !~ `BLOCKED.*` | reason !~ `CACHED.*` | unwrap duration_ms [$__range]) by ()

panels.title: Where answers came from
panels.description: Every query bucketed by what actually produced the answer. 'Cached' and 'Recursive (Unbound)' are the two that matter for cache-vs-real-lookup: anything that is not cached, blocked or conditional left the house. 'Upstream DoH (fallback)' should normally be empty — Blocky's upstream strategy is `strict`, so traffic only lands there when Unbound is failing, and a persistent band is worth chasing.

targets.expr: sum by (source) (count_over_time({job="blocky", host=~"$host"} | pattern "<_>	<client_ip>	<client_name>	<duration_ms>	<reason>	<question>	<_>" | client_name =~ `(?i).*$client.*` | label_format source=`{{ if hasPrefix "BLOCKED" .reason }}Blocked{{ else if hasPrefix "CACHED" .reason }}Cached{{ else if eq .reason "CONDITIONAL" }}Conditional (UDM Pro){{ else if hasPrefix "RESOLVED (tcp+udp:127.0.0.1:5335)" .reason }}Recursive (Unbound){{ else if hasPrefix "RESOLVED (https" .reason }}Upstream DoH (fallback){{ else if hasPrefix "RESOLVED" .reason }}Resolved (other upstream){{ else if hasPrefix "CUSTOM DNS" .reason }}Custom DNS{{ else if hasPrefix "Special-Use" .reason }}Special-use (RFC 6761){{ else }}{{ .reason }}{{ end }}` [$__auto]))

panels.title: Answer source mix
panels.description: The same breakdown totalled over the range.

targets.expr: sum by (source) (count_over_time({job="blocky", host=~"$host"} | pattern "<_>	<client_ip>	<client_name>	<duration_ms>	<reason>	<question>	<_>" | client_name =~ `(?i).*$client.*` | label_format source=`{{ if hasPrefix "BLOCKED" .reason }}Blocked{{ else if hasPrefix "CACHED" .reason }}Cached{{ else if eq .reason "CONDITIONAL" }}Conditional (UDM Pro){{ else if hasPrefix "RESOLVED (tcp+udp:127.0.0.1:5335)" .reason }}Recursive (Unbound){{ else if hasPrefix "RESOLVED (https" .reason }}Upstream DoH (fallback){{ else if hasPrefix "RESOLVED" .reason }}Resolved (other upstream){{ else if hasPrefix "CUSTOM DNS" .reason }}Custom DNS{{ else if hasPrefix "Special-Use" .reason }}Special-use (RFC 6761){{ else }}{{ .reason }}{{ end }}` [$__range]))

panels.title: Blocked vs allowed
panels.description: The headline split over time, for whatever the host and client pickers currently select.

targets.expr: sum by (status) (count_over_time({job="blocky", host=~"$host"} | pattern "<_>	<client_ip>	<client_name>	<duration_ms>	<reason>	<question>	<_>" | client_name =~ `(?i).*$client.*` | label_format status=`{{ if hasPrefix "BLOCKED" .reason }}Blocked{{ else }}Allowed{{ end }}` [$__auto]))

panels.title: Blocked vs allowed, by resolver
panels.description: Per DNS host. These are two independent resolvers, not a cluster — a client configured with both appears in both, so the two bars are not shares of one pie.

targets.expr: sum by (host, status) (count_over_time({job="blocky", host=~"$host"} | pattern "<_>	<client_ip>	<client_name>	<duration_ms>	<reason>	<question>	<_>" | client_name =~ `(?i).*$client.*` | label_format status=`{{ if hasPrefix "BLOCKED" .reason }}Blocked{{ else }}Allowed{{ end }}` [$__range]))

panels.title: Noisiest clients
panels.description: Ranked by total queries. NOT affected by the client filter — this is the panel you pick a client from.

targets.expr: topk(15, sum by (client_name) (count_over_time({job="blocky", host=~"$host"} | pattern "<_>	<client_ip>	<client_name>	<duration_ms>	<reason>	<question>	<_>" [$__range])))

panels.title: Most-blocked clients
panels.description: Ranked by blocked queries only. Also ignores the client filter. A device near the top of this and not the panel to its left is doing little else.

targets.expr: topk(15, sum by (client_name) (count_over_time({job="blocky", host=~"$host"} |= "BLOCKED" | pattern "<_>	<client_ip>	<client_name>	<duration_ms>	<reason>	<question>	<_>" | reason =~ `BLOCKED.*` [$__range])))

panels.title: Per-client breakdown
panels.description: Queries, blocked, and blocked share per client, over the range. Ignores the client filter. A client with no blocked queries has no series for those two columns, which is why they read 0 rather than being absent.

targets.expr: sum by (client_name, metric) (count_over_time({job="blocky", host=~"$host"} | pattern "<_>	<client_ip>	<client_name>	<duration_ms>	<reason>	<question>	<_>" | label_format metric=`Queries` [$__range]))

sum by (client_name, metric) (count_over_time({job="blocky", host=~"$host"} |= "BLOCKED" | pattern "<_>	<client_ip>	<client_name>	<duration_ms>	<reason>	<question>	<_>" | reason =~ `BLOCKED.*` | label_format metric=`Blocked` [$__range]))

label_replace(sum by (client_name) (count_over_time({job="blocky", host=~"$host"} |= "BLOCKED" | pattern "<_>	<client_ip>	<client_name>	<duration_ms>	<reason>	<question>	<_>" | reason =~ `BLOCKED.*` [$__range])) / sum by (client_name) (count_over_time({job="blocky", host=~"$host"} | pattern "<_>	<client_ip>	<client_name>	<duration_ms>	<reason>	<question>	<_>" [$__range])) * 100, "metric", "Blocked %", "", "")

panels.title: Queries per client over time
panels.description: The top 5 clients at each point in time, bucketed. This is the panel that shows a device that started talking at 3am and has not stopped.

targets.expr: topk(5, sum by (client_name) (count_over_time({job="blocky", host=~"$host"} | pattern "<_>	<client_ip>	<client_name>	<duration_ms>	<reason>	<question>	<_>" | client_name =~ `(?i).*$client.*` [$__auto])))

panels.title: Top blocked domains
panels.description: What the blocklists are actually catching, in the range.

targets.expr: topk(20, sum by (question) (count_over_time({job="blocky", host=~"$host"} |= "BLOCKED" | pattern "<_>	<client_ip>	<client_name>	<duration_ms>	<reason>	<question>	<_>" | client_name =~ `(?i).*$client.*` | reason =~ `BLOCKED.*` [$__range])))

panels.title: Top allowed domains
panels.description: What the house actually resolves, blocked queries excluded.

targets.expr: topk(20, sum by (question) (count_over_time({job="blocky", host=~"$host"} | pattern "<_>	<client_ip>	<client_name>	<duration_ms>	<reason>	<question>	<_>" | client_name =~ `(?i).*$client.*` | reason !~ `BLOCKED.*` [$__range])))

panels.title: Blocklist rules doing the work
panels.description: The matched rule rather than the domain — `ads: *.doubleclick.net` is one rule catching many names. Useful for spotting which list earns its place, and for finding the rule to allowlist when something legitimate breaks.

targets.expr: topk(15, sum by (rule) (count_over_time({job="blocky", host=~"$host"} |= "BLOCKED" | pattern "<_>	<client_ip>	<client_name>	<duration_ms>	<reason>	<question>	<_>" | client_name =~ `(?i).*$client.*` | reason =~ `BLOCKED.*` | label_format rule=`{{ regexReplaceAll "^BLOCKED \\((.*)\\)$" .reason "${1}" }}` [$__range])))

panels.title: Query log
panels.description: The raw query log, reformatted to one readable line. Use the client box and the blocked/allowed picker at the top to narrow it.

targets.expr: {job="blocky", host=~"$host"} | pattern "<_>	<client_ip>	<client_name>	<duration_ms>	<reason>	<question>	<_>" | client_name =~ `(?i).*$client.*` $logfilter | line_format `{{ .client_name }}  {{ .question }}  {{ .reason }}  {{ .duration_ms }}ms`

options.content:
**Source.** Blocky's own query log, shipped to Loki by Alloy (`modules/alloy.nix`).
Retention is Loki's 14 days, not Blocky's 30 on disk.

**The two resolvers are independent.** mirkwood and rivendell each log what
*they* answered. A client configured with both is counted in both, so `All`
sums rather than de-duplicates. Pick a single host for exact per-resolver
numbers.

**Only the left-hand columns are parsed, on purpose.** The log is tab-separated,
but the `answer` column is CSV-quoted and can itself contain tabs — an HTTPS/SVCB
record serialises with them. Parsing positionally past `answer` therefore
mis-assigns columns on ~1.5% of lines (it reads `IN` as the response type). Every
query here stops at `question`, which is lossless. Query type and response code
live past that break: get them from the **Blocky** dashboard, which reads
Prometheus.

**Client filter** is a case-insensitive substring — `ipad` matches
`iPad.home.theshire.io`. The two client ranking panels deliberately ignore it,
so there is always something to pick from.

**Counts are queries, not devices.** A page load is many queries, and a client
that retries a blocked name inflates its own bar — which is the honest number
for "who is making the most requests", but not for "who is busiest".

list.name: client
list.label: client contains
list.description: Case-insensitive substring. Leave empty for all.

list.name: logfilter
list.label: query log shows
list.query: All : | reason =~ `.*`,Blocked only : | reason =~ `BLOCKED.*`,Allowed only : | reason !~ `BLOCKED.*`

title: DNS — Query Analytics
